summary: Serve current work pages and windows only from the published work list, never folding it on a request

replay.detail: No claim replay or stored history changes.

schema.detail: No database schema, version or stored data changes; the list and its per-actor orders live in memory.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or coordination changes; no coordinated upgrade required.

compatibility.detail: GET /v1/client/work (current, not history) now answers from the published work list: a first page is a slice of the newest publication under its own snapshot, and a continuation keeps that publication until its cursor expires or a replay, trim or heal replaces the projections behind it. While the list has no current publication, a first page answers HTTP 503, retryable, with details.reason work-list-not-ready, and a work window gets one retryable resync and then waits for the next publication. fresh=true waits up to two seconds for a publication at the request's index, else answers 503 with details.reason work-list-not-fresh. If the work refresher stops for good, pages answer 503, not retryable, with details.reason work-list-ended, and windows get one error frame. st work ls asks for a fresh first page and retries not-ready and not-fresh answers within --daemon-wait. Error codes on the wire are unchanged (internal); the reason is in details. GET /v1/client/request-latency gains scope work-list stage rows (fresh-wait, page, actor-build), descriptive only; fresh work reads still count, wait included, under the existing person-read target. The machine contract declares fresh on work.list.

downtime.detail: Current work pages answer a retryable HTTP 503 (details.reason work-list-not-ready) until the work list's first fold after the daemon starts, and again after each replay, trim or heal and each withdrawal until the next publication; windows get one retryable resync and then their rows. st work ls retries within --daemon-wait; a client that does not retry, such as the TypeScript or Swift workList, sees the 503.

recovery.detail: Only volatile in-memory lists change; restart with ST3_PUBLISHED_LISTS=off to read current work directly.
